title: West Ham lose Andy Carroll for three months after striker’s foot surgery
trail: West Ham United will be without Andy Carroll for three months and fear Manuel Lanzini could be absent for a month after damaging a hamstring
body: West Ham United will be without Andy Carroll for three months after the striker underwent surgery on a foot injury. The club also fear Manuel Lanzini could be absent until the end of February after damaging a hamstring. The loss of the attacking pair could influence the club’s transfer policy. Carroll had hoped a period of rest, wearing a protective boot, might speed rehabilitation from the fracture, apparently sustained in the victory against West Bromwich Albion this month in which he scored his only goals of the campaign, only for a second specialist to advise surgery as the best course of action. The forward, who made a cameo appearance against Tottenham after the West Brom fixture and had been the subject of interest from Chelsea, had an operation on Monday morning and will not be available until April at best. Lanzini was substituted in the second half of the 1-1 draw with Bournemouth on Saturday after pulling up clutching his hamstring and has undergone a scan. There will be further assessments this week but he is expected to be out for at least a month. West Ham are intent upon adding to David Moyes’s options, with the manager having travelled to Spain to watch potential targets on Sunday and his assistant, Stuart Pearce, dispatched to assess Belgium’s Leander Dendoncker in Anderlecht’s victory at Genk. The 22-year-old, normally a midfielder, played at centre-half and has been tracked by a number of English clubs. There is strong interest, too, in Newcastle’s Jonjo Shelvey. In the absence of Carroll, West Ham are likely to sanction the departure of only one of their forwards and Moyes – who is close to welcoming back Michail Antonio and José Fonte to the first-team group after groin and ankle injuries respectively – is reluctant to let Javier Hernández leave. André Ayew is being targeted by his former club Swansea City and there has been interest in Diafra Sakho, who has recovered from a knee problem. The Senegalese is the likeliest of the forwards to leave.
